[\"logs\",\"--help\"].out:
Usage: stim logs [options]

Query this workspace's merged NDJSON log timeline (bundler, client, device,
build, agent actions, maintenance). Prints and exits; an existing timeline with
nothing matching is a successful, empty result. Use --follow to stream.

Options:
  --slot <name>    Only this device slot's records, plus the shared Metro and
                   app client records once it has launched
  --source <s...>  Only these sources: metro, client, device, build, agent,
                   maintenance, placement, or all; gc alone reads the
                   machine-wide gc log of what gc and maintenance cleared, and
                   builds alone reads the machine-wide ledger of native builds
  --level <l>      Minimum level: debug, info, warn, error, fatal
  --since <d>      Only records newer than this, e.g. 30s, 5m, 2h
  --grep <re>      Only records whose message matches this regular expression
  --tail <n>       Only the last n matching records
  --errors         Errors and fatals since the last marker, from metro, client
                   and build, plus confirmed native app-crash reports and stim
                   web browser errors. Add --source maintenance for maintenance
                   failures, or --source device or --source all for general
                   device errors.
  --follow         Keep streaming new records until interrupted
  --json           Emit the raw records, one per line (valid NDJSON; zero
                   matches is zero bytes, exit 0)
  -h, --help       display help for command

[\"doctor\",\"--help\"].out:
Usage: stim doctor [options]

Inspect the source checkout and report project state that can make native
worktrees slow or invalid. The checkout is left untouched unless --fix is
passed; --platform filters native findings. Each run in a supported native app
is recorded in Stim state so guide can say when doctor is due.

Options:
  --json                 print the findings as JSON
  --platform <platform>  report shared findings plus only this native platform:
                         ios or android
  --fix                  repair the sandbox allowance when the report names it,
                         and stale Android .cxx configurations in a React Native
                         or Expo checkout; install the Android system image stim
                         android would install on its first emulator run; add
                         linked worktrees nested in a checkout to its
                         .watchmanconfig ignore_dirs; in a terminal, after
                         asking about each step and its cost, bring the source
                         checkout to a state worktrees can clone (reinstall a
                         stale or missing dependency tree, run pod install
                         --clean-install and, for a conflict with a gitignored
                         Podfile.lock, pod update of only the named pods, and
                         run the prebuild Stim has no current record of, without
                         compiling); ask each remote machine in remote.machines
                         for build and device-host approval. Stop native builds
                         first. Generated CMake output must be ignored and
                         untracked; custom launcher settings and source files
                         are preserved.
  -h, --help             display help for command

[\"gc\",\"--help\"].out:
Usage: stim gc [options]

Run one automatic maintenance pass now at the measured pressure level, or the
level --pressure names, and delete what it takes. At every level: workspace
build outputs and shared caches over their caps, what the age sweep removes,
unused iOS simulator runtimes, registry entries and owned devices of removed
projects, stale records, workspace logs over their cap, finished linked
worktrees past their grace period, and every workspace idle for idle.dormantDays
reduced to its minimal size: build outputs, owned devices, and a linked
worktree's node_modules and Pods. At high, the pressure ladder to its end as
well: idle dev servers and their build outputs, parked devices, shared caches
trimmed to half their caps, idle workspaces made dormant, node_modules and Pods
of idle linked worktrees, idle Gradle daemons, unpinned Gradle versions,
temporary leftovers, and clean merged worktrees without the grace period. At
critical, every shared cache Stim registered emptied, clean pushed worktrees
idle 7 days, every device recording and archived content, then the caches of
other tools through their own commands (npm, Yarn, pnpm, CocoaPods, Gradle,
SwiftPM), which high also runs while free disk stays under disk.minFreeGb. It
never touches a workspace that is building, driven, leased, hosted or pinned by
maintenance.keep.

Options:
  --dry-run           report what the run would delete, and delete nothing
  --pressure <level>  run at this level, normal, high or critical, instead of
                      the measured one
  --json              print the result as JSON on stdout; every other line goes
                      to stderr
  -h, --help          display help for command

[\"device\",\"--help\"].out:
Usage: stim device [options] [command]

Lease a connected physical device to this workspace, give it back, provision iOS
signing for it, or change the workspace's own simulator or emulator

Options:
  -h, --help                                          display help for command

Commands:
  lock [options] <platform> [id]                      Lease a connected physical device, or this workspace's own simulator or emulator, to this workspace for a declared time, so another workspace's `--device` run waits and agents see the device as driven. Nothing but this command and a `--device` run moves the expiry.
  unlock [options] [platform]                         Release the device lease or leases this workspace holds. Releasing nothing is not an error.
  provision [options] <platform> [udid]               Register a connected iPhone with the project's Apple Developer team and create or refresh its iOS App Development profile, through xcodebuild -allowProvisioningUpdates. It lists the account changes and asks first; no build ever does this.
  location [options] <platform>                       Set or clear the simulated location of this workspace's own simulator or emulator. Android cannot clear one.
  permission [options] <platform> <action> <service>  Grant, revoke or reset one privacy permission for the app on this workspace's own simulator or emulator. Android reads the grant state back; iOS has no read.
  push [options] <platform>                           Send a test push notification to the app on this workspace's own iOS simulator.
  network [options] <platform> <state>                Turn Wi-Fi and mobile data on or off on this workspace's own Android emulator, and read them back.
  help [command]                                      display help for command

[\"share\",\"--help\"].out:
Usage: stim share [options] <action>

Share this workspace's running app through a public web link, with a generated
password unless you set or drop it: share ios|android starts one (and the server
inside stimd, when it does not run), share stop ends this workspace's shares,
share list lists this Stim home's shares. Every share's link and password are
saved for share ios|android --reuse, which starts a stopped share again until it
expires (a new share, with a warning, when nothing is saved); share stop
--forget deletes them.

Options:
  --slot <name>            Share the device of this slot
  --device                 Share the physical device this workspace leases
                           instead of its simulator or emulator
  --control                Let viewers tap, type and press buttons (watch only
                           without it)
  --password <value>       Use this password (8 to 128 characters) instead of a
                           generated one
  --no-password            Need no password: anyone with the link can open the
                           share
  --view-password [value]  With --control, a second password that only watches
                           (8 to 128 characters, generated without a value)
  --slug <name>            Use /s/<name>/ as the link instead of a random token
                           (3 to 32 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; needs
                           a password)
  --reuse                  Start the saved link and passwords of this
                           workspace's last share of this target again, until it
                           expires, or start a new share with a warning when
                           nothing is saved (a saved share takes no --control,
                           --password, --no-password, --view-password or --slug;
                           --expires replaces the expiry)
  --forget                 With stop, also delete this workspace's saved links
                           so --reuse has nothing to start
  --expires <minutes>      Minutes until the share ends, 1 to 480 (default 60;
                           with --reuse, the saved expiry)
  --json                   Emit one JSON payload
  -h, --help               display help for command

[\"start\",\"--help\"].out:
Usage: stim start [options]

Start this workspace's dev server, run by this home's stimd, and wait until it
verifies as this project's. Idempotent: a healthy dev server on the reserved
port is a no-op. Structured logs land in the global workspace logs directory.

Options:
  --json            Emit the facts as a single JSON line on stdout; every other
                    line goes to stderr
  --wait <seconds>  How long to wait for the dev server to answer (default 60)
  --remote          Prepare the dev server for a remote device
  --reset-cache     Restart owned Metro and clear this app's Metro caches
  -h, --help        display help for command

[\"stop\",\"--help\"].out:
Usage: stim stop [options]

The inverse of `start`: halt this workspace's supervisor, shut the owned device
down (never deleted), and free the reserved port. Non-destructive -- the device
stays assigned, so coming back costs a boot, except that an owned iOS simulator
stays booted for pool.bootedGraceMinutes when memory permits. Acts on the
current workspace.

Options:
  --slot <name>  Stop only this device slot, keeping the shared server running.
                 Use 'default' for the workspace's default device, or 'web' to
                 close only the owned Chrome.
  --json         print the per-step outcomes as JSON
  -h, --help     display help for command

[\"ios\",\"--help\"].out:
Usage: stim ios [options]

Build (or restore from the fingerprint cache), install and launch this
workspace's app on its owned simulator. React Native and Expo Debug runs start
the dev server when it is not running.

Options:
  --eas-profile <name>    Download a matching EAS development build; on a miss,
                          print the build command without running it
  --slot <name>           Reusable device slot within this workspace (default:
                          default)
  --remote-build <value>  Build on local, auto, remote (remote machines first),
                          remote-only (never here), or one named machine; a name
                          refuses without fallback
  --json                  Emit the facts as a single JSON line on stdout; every
                          other line goes to stderr
  --plan                  Predict the next build without building, booting or
                          installing: resolve the fingerprint, check the local
                          then remote cache, and print the expected cache result
                          and duration. Writes no Stim state.
  --scheme <name>         Shared Xcode app scheme to build; overrides automatic
                          scheme selection, not the app URL scheme
  --no-metro-check        Skip the "is this workspace's dev server running?"
                          check: do not start it, and build anyway
  --no-build-cache        Build fresh, ignoring cached artifacts (local and the
                          project's build-cache provider); the fresh build still
                          replaces the cache entry
  --configuration <name>  Xcode configuration to build (e.g. Release). A
                          non-Debug configuration embeds the JS bundle and skips
                          Metro entirely. Overrides the ios.configuration
                          setting. Default: Debug
  --device-type <name>    Simulator model to create this workspace's owned sim
                          as, exactly as `xcrun simctl list devicetypes` names
                          it (e.g. "iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)"). Overrides the
                          ios.deviceType setting for this invocation. A model no
                          installed runtime can create refuses with STIM_BAD_ARG
                          and prints the models they do offer.
  --runtime <version>     Simulator runtime to create this workspace's owned sim
                          on, as a version ("18.5") or a runtime's full name
                          ("iOS 18.5"); nothing else matches. Overrides the
                          ios.runtime setting for this invocation. An unknown
                          version refuses with STIM_BAD_ARG and prints the
                          installed runtimes.
  --install-runtime       Install the explicitly requested missing iOS runtime
                          with Xcode on the local or named approved Mac (about
                          8-10 GB; shared by all workspaces)
  --simulator-app <app>   Open the owned simulator in xcode, siniulator, or
                          stim-desktop for this run, or none to open no viewer,
                          overriding the machine iosSimulatorApp setting. Also
                          opens an already running simulator; local simulators
                          only.
  --device [udid]         Build the iphoneos slice for a connected iPhone,
                          install it, and launch it, instead of using this
                          workspace's owned simulator. The phone can be cabled
                          or paired over Wi-Fi. With no UDID, the first cabled
                          device this workspace can lease is used, waiting for
                          one that is busy; a Wi-Fi device is used only when no
                          cabled one is connected and ready. In Debug the app is
                          wired to this workspace's Metro over the LAN. Stim
                          never creates, boots, or deletes a physical device.
  --remote <target>       Run on eas, proxy, or an approved Mac in
                          remote.machines; named Macs never fall back locally.
                          auto places on an approved Mac when this machine is
                          full or busy. remote tries remote.machines in order
                          first and runs here only when none takes it.
                          remote-only never runs here. local runs here, whatever
                          ios.remote says.
  --wait <seconds>        How long to wait for another workspace to release the
                          phone it leases, before refusing with STIM_DEVICE_BUSY
                          (default 60, 0 refuses at once). Without --device,
                          bound the owned-device slot wait; without --wait, a
                          queued run waits while the devices ahead of it are
                          listed, and refuses after 90 minutes or once the
                          devices cannot be counted for max(10 minutes, position
                          x 5 minutes) (--no-wait refuses immediately).
  --no-wait               Install on a phone another workspace leases instead of
                          waiting: this run takes no lease and, when both
                          workspaces build the same app id, the install
                          terminates the holder's running app. Without --device,
                          refuse a full device cap or existing slot queue
                          immediately.
  -h, --help              display help for command

[\"android\",\"--help\"].out:
Usage: stim android [options]

Build (or install from the shared cache), install and launch this workspace's
Android app on its owned emulator. React Native and Expo Debug runs start the
dev server when it is not running.

Options:
  --eas-profile <name>    Download a matching EAS development build; on a miss,
                          print the build command without running it
  --slot <name>           Reusable device slot within this workspace (default:
                          default)
  --remote-build <value>  Build on local, auto, remote (remote machines first),
                          remote-only (never here), or one named machine; a name
                          refuses without fallback
  --json                  Emit the facts as a single JSON line on stdout; every
                          other line goes to stderr
  --plan                  Predict the next build without building, booting or
                          installing: resolve the fingerprint, check the local
                          then remote cache, and print the expected cache result
                          and duration. Writes no Stim state.
  --no-metro-check        Skip the reserved-port Metro health check and do not
                          start it (the app will load no bundle unless something
                          else serves it)
  --no-build-cache        Build fresh, ignoring cached artifacts (local and the
                          project's build-cache provider); the fresh build still
                          replaces the cache entry
  --variant <name>        Gradle variant to assemble and install (e.g.
                          productionDebug on a flavored project); overrides the
                          android.variant setting. A variant ending in Release
                          embeds the JS bundle and skips Metro entirely.
                          Default: debug
  --system-image <id>     Android system image to create this workspace's owned
                          AVD from, as the sdkmanager package id (e.g.
                          "system-images;android-36;google_apis;arm64-v8a").
                          Overrides the android.systemImage setting for this
                          invocation. An unknown id refuses with STIM_BAD_ARG
                          and prints the installed images.
  --device-profile <id>   Hardware profile to create this workspace's owned AVD
                          with, as an `avdmanager list device -c` id (e.g.
                          "pixel_fold", "pixel_tablet"). Overrides the
                          android.deviceProfile setting for this invocation. An
                          unknown id refuses with STIM_BAD_ARG and prints the
                          available ids.
  --device [serial]       Install and launch on a connected physical device
                          instead of this workspace's owned emulator. With no
                          serial, the first connected device this workspace can
                          lease is used. Stim never creates, boots, or deletes a
                          physical device.
  --remote <target>       Run on eas, proxy, or a named approved Mac from
                          remote.machines; auto places on an approved Mac when
                          this machine is full or busy; remote tries
                          remote.machines in order first and runs here only when
                          none takes it; remote-only never runs here; local runs
                          here, whatever android.remote says
  --wait <seconds>        How long to wait for another workspace to release the
                          device it leases, before refusing with
                          STIM_DEVICE_BUSY (default 60, 0 refuses at once).
                          Without --device, bound the owned-device slot wait;
                          without --wait, a queued run waits while the devices
                          ahead of it are listed, and refuses after 90 minutes
                          or once the devices cannot be counted for max(10
                          minutes, position x 5 minutes) (--no-wait refuses
                          immediately).
  --no-wait               Install on a device another workspace leases instead
                          of waiting: this run takes no lease and, when both
                          workspaces build the same app id, the install
                          terminates the holder's running app. Without --device,
                          refuse a full device cap or existing slot queue
                          immediately.
